disclaimer: Everything on this page is a proposal or a judgement unless it is explicitly marked as sourced. No topic here has been written, and none of them is a claim about a product.

There is no keyword-volume data anywhere in this repository, and none was invented for this page. Any statement about what people search for is labelled as judgement and is an argument from the product's own documentation, not a measurement. Publishing estimated search volumes without a measurement tool would be the exact failure this project exists to avoid.

Every article proposed here is buildable from official manufacturer pages and owner's manuals only. None of them requires a hands-on test, and none may claim one: the FTC warns that you cannot talk about your experience with a product you have not tried (S8).
Each row names the official source the finished article would have to cite. If a row's sources cannot support its headline, the headline has to change - not the citation.
demand_note: Demand is argued, not measured. This page has no access to a keyword tool, an Associates reports feed or any analytics. The 'why it could earn traffic' column is reasoning about what a documented product difference answers, and it is labelled as judgement everywhere it appears.

topics.title: Can you leave a probe in an air fryer? What the manuals actually say
topics.hook: The appliance is built to run unattended. A wireless probe is built to be left in. Whether the two go together is a question the documents can answer.
topics.angle: A reader who owns any of the three products has the same follow-up question: how do I know the chicken is done without opening the door. What this site can answer today is what the manuals and brand pages of the three air fryers say about the cavity, the rack positions and leaving the unit running — plus the fact that CHEF iQ lists air-fryer use among the iQ Sense's own heat environments (S39). What it will not do is assert a clearance, a maximum probe temperature inside a specific oven, or that any brand approves the pairing: no document read here states any of those, so those cells stay unwritten and the article says why.
topics.why_it_could_earn_traffic: Judgement, not measurement: it is the question that follows a purchase of a basket or oven-style air fryer, this site already holds the manufacturer documents on both sides of it, and nothing published here answers it yet.

cadence.status: operating plan, not a scheduled autonomous publisher
cadence.rhythm: Review source changes weekly; prepare at most one useful new or substantially refreshed guide every two weeks. Publish only after primary-source, disclosure, link and build checks pass.
cadence.seasonal: Review gift and sale-checking guides ahead of the relevant retail season. The November 2026 selection is editorial context, not proof of search demand or a deal.
cadence.kill_rule: Do not publish a second article answering the same question. Improve the existing canonical guide instead. Hold a draft if its claims require unverified identity, unauthorised API content or invented first-party results.
cadence.measurement: Once authorised Search Console and first-party aggregates exist, review query impressions, clicks and guide-to-product actions over a dated comparable period before changing priorities. There is currently no such dataset.
